newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds end slightly lower.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended slightly lower in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Friday.

"Treasury bill yields and bond prices were marked down slightly today in moderate trade in sympathy with a hike in the interbank rate. But activity was limited by a shortage of players as most people have closed their books for the weekend," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.05.2.00 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 2.13/2.08 percent.
One-year closed at a yield of 2.35/2.30 percent against Thursday's yield of 2.37/2.32 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.00/98.05 from Thursday's close of S$98.03/98.08, September 2001 at S$97.08/97.13 vesus S$97.15/97.20 and June 2003 at S$95.05/95.10 against $95.15/95.20.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-3/4 percent from Thursday's 3-5/8 percent.
